title: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at distance exactly two as at distance one. The first lesson shows by arc deletion that a minimal counterexample is strongly connected and satisfies a strict deficit |F^2(S) minus F(S)| < |F(S) minus S| for every nonempty proper vertex set. The second blows up each vertex into a transitive tournament and obtains strictly concave growth |U| + |F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)|. The third proves a pruning theorem for two families of ordered pairs by bounding a matching through ranks of matrices with generic coefficients, with full proofs of Berge's lemma and Koenig's theorem. The fourth rules out strictly concave growth by an extremal choice of two families of pairs, proves the theorem, and derives the arc- and vertex-weighted forms, a balanced weighting, and the consequences for directed triangles, including the sharp girth-four case of the Behzad-Chartrand-Wall bound.

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch sy_checks.py and sy_checks2.py, outputs sy_checks.out and sy_checks2.out, 9 Oct 2026, 0 problems): the theorem on all 59,809 oriented graphs with at most 5 vertices and 20,000 random ones with 6 to 9 vertices; every identity and inclusion of the arc-deletion step (Lemma 3.1 of the first lesson) in 21,328 configurations; the blow-up estimate of Proposition 2.2 of the second lesson in 11,032 configurations and Lemma 1.3 for all subsets with m <= 6; for 1,500 random relations and families, the matching bound |M| <= |Z| + |H|, the Koenig cover, the resulting pruning bound with conflict-free members kept, NL = AB, the generic ranks of L and N, and the kernel identity of Lemma 3.7; the setup identities of Theorem 2.1 of the fourth lesson (columns proper, diagonal in R and C and conflict-free, H outside the old images) for 591 compatible pairs; the arc-weighted form, the level blow-up counts and the balanced weighting (by linear programming) on 1,500 random graphs; the circulant examples of girth four and the degree bound without triangles; Example 3.3 and Exercises 4.2, 4.3 of the second lesson, Exercises 4.1, 4.2 of the third and 6.1, 6.2 of the fourth.
checks.lint: sy_lint.py and sy_bs_scan.py (scratch): headings, provenance line, balanced TeX delimiters, every sibling and course link resolved, no backslash artefacts or control characters; 0 problems.
checks.source_reading: OpenAI preprint 'A proof of Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture' (23 Sep 2026), TeX read in full (introduction, reduction, pruning, extremal contradiction, weighted and directed-cycle consequences; library copy openai-math-20261006); every step rederived. The weighted forms are proved directly from the theorem (level blow-up, limits, and a separation argument written in the lesson) instead of through Seacrest's equivalences. Seacrest (2 arXiv papers), Brantner-Brockman-Kay-Snively, Huang-Peng, Sadhukhan-Sandeep-Sen, Sullivan (arXiv), Edmonds (NBS Journal of Research, open) and Koenig (REAL-J, open) cited by free versions; Dean-Latka, Fisher, Havet-Thomasse, Chen-Shen-Yuster, Kaneko-Locke, Caccetta-Haggkvist and Behzad-Chartrand-Wall named for credit only.
